correctness.rationale: The infectious core is an irreducible Metzler system whose disease-free spectral bound has the same sign as the source's next-generation threshold. A positive left Perron functional has derivative equal to the linear spectral term minus the strictly nonnegative standard-incidence defect. At the critical threshold that defect is strictly positive whenever any of E, I1, or I2 is positive. LaSalle then removes the infectious core, and the downstream cancer and recovered compartments decay as stable linear filters. An explicit critical left-null vector and determinant identity are independently checked symbolically.

value.rationale: The unit reproduction threshold is the exact epidemiological boundary between linear decay and invasion. The source proves global extinction only below it while separately placing a forward bifurcation at the boundary. Closing the nonhyperbolic equality case gives a complete disease-free threshold and identifies the mechanism: depletion of the susceptible fraction below one creates strict nonlinear decay even when the critical linear mode is neutral.
